question: Why is delegation such a helpful skill for nurses on a busy ward?

options.A: It allows nurses to manage workload by sharing routine care tasks safely
options.B: It prevents junior staff from learning advanced clinical procedures
options.C: It eliminates the need for any direct patient assessment by the nurse
options.D: It completely removes nursing liability from ward management

explanation: Delegation isn't about passing the buck; it's about teamwork! It helps spread out daily care duties so every patient gets timely attention. [learn more](GST321_U1_T15#GST321_U1_T15_h1)

question: Which of the following is one of the famous 'five rights' of clinical delegation?
explanation: Always remember the five rights: right task, right circumstance, right person, right direction, and right supervision! [learn more](GST321_U1_T15#GST321_U1_T15_h2)

question: A nurse tells an assistant to check vital signs on a stable patient and report back immediately if anything changes. Which right of delegation is this?
explanation: Giving clear, concise instructions and letting the person know exactly what to report is all about getting the 'right direction' step right. [learn more](GST321_U1_T15#GST321_U1_T15_h2)

question: What is the golden rule for someone receiving a delegated task (the delegatee)?

options.A: To independently change the patient care plan if complications arise
options.B: To accept only tasks within their training and scope of practice
options.C: To take over full legal liability for the entire ward
options.D: To perform advanced clinical assessments on unstable patients

explanation: Safety first! A delegatee should only ever take on tasks they have been properly trained and authorized to perform. [learn more](GST321_U1_T15#GST321_U1_T15_h3)

question: What should an auxiliary nurse do if asked to perform a procedure they have never been taught?

options.A: Refuse the task and inform the nurse of their lack of training
options.B: Ignore the instruction and leave the ward immediately
options.C: Attempt the procedure quietly to avoid upsetting senior staff
options.D: Ask another patient to guide them through the steps

explanation: It takes courage, but speaking up keeps patients safe. Never attempt unfamiliar clinical procedures without proper training. [learn more](GST321_U1_T15#GST321_U1_T15_h3)

question: Why is patient stability so important when deciding whether or not to delegate a task?

options.A: Stable patients do not require any monitoring from healthcare workers
options.B: Unstable patients always pay more for hospital accommodation
options.C: Stable patients are harder to communicate with than unstable ones
options.D: Unstable patients require continuous clinical judgment that only a registered nurse can provide

explanation: When a patient's condition can change rapidly, it needs a professional nurse's close assessment rather than auxiliary care. [learn more](GST321_U1_T15#GST321_U1_T15_h4)

question: Which of these tasks is generally NOT okay to delegate to an auxiliary nurse?

options.A: Measuring and recording routine weight on a admission scale
options.B: Formulating an initial nursing care plan for a newly admitted patient
options.C: Feeding a patient who has a stable swallowing reflex
options.D: Assisting a mobile patient with walking to the bathroom

explanation: Care planning requires professional clinical assessment and critical thinking, which stays with the registered nurse. [learn more](GST321_U1_T15#GST321_U1_T15_h4)

question: What is the main downside when a nurse suffers from 'under-delegation' (refusing to delegate tasks)?

options.A: Excessive free time for nursing assistants on the ward
options.B: Burnout and exhaustion from trying to perform all tasks personally
options.C: Immediate legal prosecution for negligence by the hospital board
options.D: Complete elimination of patient care errors in the facility

explanation: Trying to do everything yourself on a shift is a fast track to burnout. Trust your team and share the load! [learn more](GST321_U1_T15#GST321_U1_T15_h5)

question: What do we call it when a nurse dumps way too many duties onto assistants, making safe care impossible?
explanation: Over-delegation happens when team members are stretched too thin beyond safe limits. Balance is key in ward management. [learn more](GST321_U1_T15#GST321_U1_T15_h5)

question: What does proper supervision actually look like after you delegate a task?

options.A: Leaving the hospital premises while work is ongoing
options.B: Taking over all patient documentation duties entirely
options.C: Writing a daily report without visiting the ward
options.D: Guiding, monitoring, and inspecting the performance of the delegatee

explanation: Supervision means staying connected! You check in, offer guidance, and make sure everything went smoothly. [learn more](GST321_U1_T15#GST321_U1_T15_h6)

question: A nurse asks an assistant to give a bed bath, and later checks on the patient to see if they are comfortable. What step of delegation is this?
explanation: Checking back on the patient and reviewing how the task was done completes the supervision and evaluation loop! [learn more](GST321_U1_T15#GST321_U1_T15_h6)
